full_judgment: 14. It is also evident from the trial court's order No. 8 dated 1-8-2005 where the learned trial judge directed upon the pre-emptee No. 2 to provide with the foreign address of the pre-emptee No. 1, but no order of the trial court shows that he directed to provide with the address of the pre-emptee No. 3 namely Md Layed Ahmed. But astonishingly from the trial court's order No. 17 dated 5-6-2006 which states  “...... আগামী ৫-৯-২০০৬ ইং তারিখ আপত্তি দাখিল । ধার্য তাং ৩/২৪ নং তরফছানীর এ/ডি ফেরত । পরবর্তীতে দেখা যায় যে, ৩নং তরফছানীর এডি ফেরত আসিয়াছে ।......" In the record there is nothing to indicate that service of summons was made upon the pre-emptee No. 3 at his address in Saudi Arabia, nor the acknowledgment due (A/D) was received by the trial court from the pre-emptee No. 3 who lives in Saudi Arabia. Above all, the pre-emptor admitted in his cross-examination that he did not serve any summons upon the pre-emptee No. 3 at the address in Saudia Arabia. Accordingly it is not safe to rely on statutory presumption of service of summon, upon the pre-emptee No. 3 within the meaning of Order V Rule 19 B(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the present case a judgment and order of pre-emption was obtained which indicates that a fraud was committed upon the court in the service of summon upon the pre-emptee No. 3. When a fraud is proved, then that fraud vitiates everything.
